blocks.text: Tree of thoughts, ToT, extends chain of thought, covered earlier in this module, from a single linear reasoning path into a branching tree of possibilities, exploring several candidate next steps at each point, evaluating them, and pruning away the weaker ones before continuing.

This topic covers how tree of thoughts structures exploration as branches rather than one chain, how weak branches get pruned and strong ones get continued, how it differs from self-consistency, and the real orchestration complexity involved in actually implementing it.
1. What Tree of Thoughts Means

blocks.alt: Building on self-consistency prompting, tree of thoughts introduces branching exploration

blocks.text: Tree of thoughts treats problem solving as a search over a tree of possible reasoning steps, rather than committing to one single reasoning chain the way plain chain of thought does, at each step, several candidate next thoughts get generated, evaluated, and the more promising ones get explored further.
2. From a Single Chain to a Branching Tree

blocks.alt: Chain of thought follows one linear path, tree of thoughts branches into multiple paths

blocks.text: Where chain of thought, covered in an earlier topic, commits to one reasoning path from start to finish, tree of thoughts allows the reasoning process to branch at any point where multiple different next steps seem plausible, keeping several possibilities alive simultaneously rather than choosing just one early on.
3. Generating Multiple Candidate Next Steps

blocks.alt: A starting thought branches into branch A, branch B, and branch C

blocks.text: At each node in the tree, the model generates several distinct candidate next thoughts, rather than just one, each representing a different possible direction the reasoning could take from that point.

scored = [(c, evaluate(c)) for c in candidates]
best_candidates = sorted(scored, key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)[:2]

blocks.text: 4. Evaluating and Pruning Branches

blocks.alt: Each branch gets evaluated, a weak branch gets pruned, a strong branch gets kept

blocks.text: After generating candidate branches, each one gets evaluated, either by the model itself judging its own promise, or by an external scoring function, weaker branches get pruned away, and only the more promising ones continue to be explored further, this pruning is what keeps the tree from growing unmanageably large.

blocks.text: 5. Backtracking When a Branch Dead-Ends

blocks.alt: A branch that reaches a dead end triggers backtracking to an earlier node, then trying a different branch

blocks.text: A genuine advantage tree of thoughts has over a single chain, if a branch turns out to be a dead end, the exploration can backtrack to an earlier node and try a different branch instead, a single chain of thought attempt has no such recovery option once it commits to a bad early step.

blocks.title: This backtracking ability is the core structural advantage
blocks.content: Plain chain of thought has no way to recover from an early misstep, tree of thoughts explicit branching and backtracking is specifically designed to give the reasoning process a way out of a path that stops making progress.

blocks.text: 6. Tree of Thoughts vs Self-Consistency

blocks.alt: Self-consistency votes across independent full paths, tree of thoughts explores and prunes step by step

blocks.text: Self-consistency, covered in the previous topic, runs several complete, independent reasoning attempts and votes on the final answer, tree of thoughts instead evaluates and prunes at every intermediate step along the way, making it a more fine grained, but also more computationally involved, form of exploration.
7. The Real Cost, Many More Model Calls Than CoT

Because tree of thoughts generates multiple candidates at every node and evaluates each one, it requires substantially more model calls than a single chain of thought pass, or even self-consistency, this cost scales with both the branching factor and the depth of the tree explored.
8. When Tree of Thoughts Is Genuinely Worth It

blocks.alt: A complex planning or puzzle task justifies the cost of ToT, a simple direct task makes it unnecessary overhead

blocks.text: Tree of thoughts earns its substantial cost on genuinely complex planning problems and puzzles, where a wrong early step can derail an entire chain of thought attempt and multiple plausible paths genuinely exist to explore, for straightforward tasks, this level of exploration is unnecessary overhead.
9. Implementing Tree of Thoughts Requires Orchestration Logic

Unlike chain of thought, which can be triggered with a simple prompt phrase, tree of thoughts requires actual orchestration code, managing the tree structure, generating candidates, scoring them, and deciding when to prune or backtrack, this is meaningfully more implementation work than the simpler techniques covered earlier in this module.
Worked Example

A team building a logic puzzle solver finds that chain of thought frequently commits to a promising looking first move that turns out to be a dead end partway through, requiring a full restart from scratch.

Implementing tree of thoughts, generating several candidate first moves, evaluating each for how much progress it makes toward a solution, and backtracking to try an alternative branch when one dead-ends, solves noticeably more puzzles correctly than the single chain of thought approach, at the cost of substantially more model calls per puzzle solved.
Common Mistakes

items: Using tree of thoughts for a simple, direct task where the substantial extra cost provides no real accuracy benefit
Underestimating the orchestration complexity required to actually implement branching, evaluation, and pruning logic
Letting the tree grow too wide or too deep without effective pruning, causing costs to spiral
Confusing tree of thoughts with self-consistency, which votes across full independent paths rather than pruning at each step

blocks.text: Practice

Take a puzzle or planning problem with several plausible early approaches, sketch out by hand what a tree of thoughts exploration would look like, which branches you would generate, how you would evaluate them, and where backtracking would likely be needed.
Key Takeaway

Tree of thoughts extends chain of thought into a branching search, generating multiple candidate reasoning steps at each point, evaluating and pruning weaker branches, and backtracking from dead ends, a powerful but substantially more costly and implementation heavy technique best reserved for genuinely complex planning and puzzle solving tasks.
